exposure: Cerebral blood flow values in basal ganglia (caudate nuclei, lenticular nuclei), thalami, and white matter regions measured by three-dimensional pseudo-continuous arterial spin labelling (3-D pcASL) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
outcome: Neurobehavioral outcomes (favourable vs. adverse) assessed by Neonatal Behavioral Neurological Assessment scores
cohort: Twenty-three full-term neonates diagnosed with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) who underwent MRI (conventional and 3-D pcASL perfusion MRI).
finding: The average cerebral blood flow in the basal ganglia and thalami measured by 3-D pcASL perfusion MRI was significantly higher in the adverse neurobehavioral outcome group (37.28+-6.42 ml/100 g/min) compared to the favourable outcome group (22.55 +- 3.21 ml/100 g/min), indicating its potential for early prediction of outcomes in neonates with HIE.
